title: The Roman Soldier Who Wrote Home Asking for Socks
notes: Lighter register than Days 1 and 2. speaking_rate is 0.95, slightly brisker, and pauses are shorter overall. If a music bed is ever used on this channel, this is the video it suits.
Tablet 291 (Claudia Severa's birthday invitation) is on Commons and is the centrepiece (p12). It is used twice: introduced at s30, returned to for the handwriting reveal at s35-s38.
Tablet 346 (the socks letter) is NOT on Commons. The cold open and s27-s28 use general tablet photographs instead. Do not label any image on screen as Tablet 346.

The child's shoe (p07) is from Vindolanda itself and is dated c. 200-213 AD - later than the c. AD 100 tablets. It illustrates 'shoes in every size including children's', which is accurate; do not caption it with a date that implies it is contemporary with the letters.
Heavy use of CC BY-SA. Every one requires attribution. The credits card for this video is longer than usual.
Every archival URL was resolved from the Commons API and checked live.
LOW RESOLUTION: both 'Detail from Roman fort of Vindolanda' images (p06, p14) are only about 30KB. Show them as small cards at native size, no upscaling.
v3: generated tablets are always blank or closed and tied, never shown with writing and never presented as a specific numbered tablet. The real tablets appear only as photo cards.
v3: Roman soldiers, the Batavians, Claudia Severa and Sulpicia Lepidina appear in illustrations only from behind, in silhouette or with faces turned away.

scenes: a muddy waterlogged trench on a green northern English hillside in 1973, an archaeologist seen from behind kneeling with a trowel
a hand lifting a thin dark sliver of wood like a wood shaving out of grey clay
a single thin dark sliver of waterlogged wood lying on wet clay, about the size of a postcard, glistening, close view
the sliver hovering over a spoil heap, about to be tossed away
two thin wooden leaves being gently peeled apart by fingertips, faint dark marks glimpsed inside
beats.note: First sight of the writing. Cut in on 'there was writing inside'.

scenes: a reed pen and a tiny ink pot on a rough table, warm firelight
a pair of plain woollen socks springing out of a parcel like a reveal
a parcel wrapped in cloth and cord being opened on a wooden table, hands only
a neat flat lay of woollen socks, two pairs of leather sandals and two pairs of linen underpants
a row of soldiers in a barrack room seen from behind, sharing a fire
a sealed envelope-like wooden tablet alone on a table, its edges blurred into shadow
a faint map with one place-name dot glowing and everything around it blank
Roman rubbish being tipped into a ditch at the edge of a timber fort
a ditch sealed under layers of wet clay, a thin tablet trapped in the darkness
hundreds of thin dark wooden slivers laid out in rows on pale archival trays under even light, seen from above, orderly
beats.title_overlay: The Roman Soldier Who Wrote Home Asking for Socks
beats.note: Build the title over this during the 2s pause after s08.

scenes: a timber Roman fort on a cold green hill in northern Britain, smoke from chimneys, seen from far above
a stone wall snaking over crags into the distance, seen from the air
a minimal cartographic map of northern Britain on aged paper, a hairline drawn across the narrow neck of the island, a single ink dot a little south of it
a timeline drawn as a road: a small timber fort first, a stone wall rising much later
the edge of a hand-drawn map dissolving into blank parchment beyond a line of tiny forts
beats.note: The dot is Vindolanda; the line is where the Wall will later go. The point is that the dot came first.

scenes: a minimal map of north-west Europe on aged paper, a faint red route running from a river delta on the continent across the sea to the north of Britain
auxiliary soldiers seen from behind marching along a muddy road under grey skies, shields on their backs
a distant marble city glowing far away across a map, the soldiers' road never reaching it
a magnifying glass sweeping over a cross-section of earth
soldiers seen from behind flattening an old timber fort and spreading turf and clay over the debris
layer after layer of fort and clay stacking upward like a cake, seen in cross-section
a clay seal closing over a layer, tiny bubbles of air being pushed out
a cross-section of excavated earth showing distinct dark and pale horizontal layers of clay and turf, a sliver of dark wood visible in one band, soft side light
tiny cartoon bacteria stopped at a sealed clay barrier, unable to reach a leather shoe
a heap of ancient leather shoes of every size laid out on a museum table, from large boots to tiny ones
a wooden comb and a coil of horse harness on dark cloth
beats.note: A child's shoe. Lands on 'in every size including children's'. Hold it.

scenes: thin slivers of birch and alder being shaved from a log with a knife, hands only
a reed pen dipping into ink beside a folded, tied wooden tablet
a monumental carved stone panel on one side and a scrappy folded note on a kitchen table on the other
a note left beside a bread loaf and a cup on a rough table in morning light
a stack of folded wooden tablets on a camp desk with a yawning cat beside it
a clerk seen from behind counting soldiers on an abacus by lamplight
a row of beds in a sick bay with one blanket drawn up, nobody visible
soldiers seen from behind lined up at a morning roll call in drizzle
a single tablet slightly sticking out of a tidy stack, glowing faintly
a small pile of opened oyster shells on a rough wooden board beside a clay cup, soft window light
a soldier seen from behind standing stiffly before an officer's desk, holding a small folded tablet
a single folded wooden writing tablet tied with a thin cord, resting on a rough wooden table, close view, a cold draught of light across it
a row of plain clay drinking vessels on a wooden shelf, one tipped on its side and empty
beats.note: Light beat. Hard cut for comic timing.

scenes: misty northern hills beyond a palisade, figures far away on the far ridge in silhouette
an officer seen from behind writing at a lamplit desk, the window full of dark hills
beats.note: The frontier itself. The other side of it is where the Brittunculi lived.

scenes: a giant marble empire map shrinking down to a single candle on one desk

scenes: an archive drawer opening with a handful of the very first tablets found

scenes: a lamplit room in a Roman commander's house at the edge of the frontier, a desk by a window
